Oglethorpe Estate Main House places guests within convenient reach of Savannah’s most recognizable historic sites and downtown destinations. Oglethorpe Estate places you within easy reach of many of Savannah’s most recognizable historic sites and downtown destinations. text: A Tiny Home with A Big History

Greene Square is one of Savannah's many green spots, and it was established in 1799 as a tribute to General Nathanael Greene, who was a hero of the American Revolution. Greene Square went on to be a central place for African-American culture, including the Second African Baptist Church, which is located just outside of it. Inside the square, you'll find carefully-manicured walkways surrounded by trees and shrubs. The lawn is a great place to bring a blanket and have a picnic, or you can simply sit on one of the benches in the square and watch the nearby streets.

text: The Wonders of the Historic District

It doesn’t get much better than the Historic District when you’re looking for incredible places to stay while visiting Savannah. All the special landmarks and amazing parks that make Georgia vacations so memorable will be right at your fingertips when you make this neighborhood your home for a few nights. Some of the popular landmarks that are just a few steps away from the home include the Green-Meldrim Home, Chippewa Square, Forsyth Park and the Juliette Gordon Low Birthplace. Any savvy traveler will tell you that Georgia vacations just aren't complete if they don't include Savannah. The city is home to 22 historic squares that rival anything you'll find in Europe's iconic cities. The city's rich history also speaks through its historic cemeteries. The graves at well-known attractions like Colonial Park Cemetery, Bonaventure Cemetery and Laurel Grove Cemetery serve as the final resting places for English settlers, Confederate soldiers and African American slaves. In addition to popular landmarks right near the Historic District, you'll be able to easily get to Wormsloe Plantation and the Telfair Museum of Art. Of course, Abercorn Common, Oglethorpe Mall and Abercorn Walk are the best shopping centers in the city. Of all the vacation homes Savannah tourists have to choose from, none can set the mood for history, relaxation and adventure quite like this home can.

You can even consider taking a ferry from downtown's riverwalk to Hutchinson Island. When seeking more excursions, add pub crawls, fun trolley tours, and haunted cemetery tours to the list of adventures that show off all of the thrills and delights of Savannah. Finally, Savannah is a fantastic place to catch a festival. The list of festivals that attract visitors from around the country each year includes the Savannah Jazz Festival, the Savannah Craft Brew Fest, the Savannah Film Festival, and the Pin Point Seafood Festival.

The bustling, cobbled streets and sidewalks of Savannah downtown truly offer something for everyone. If you're looking for a cultural experience to rival anything you'd find in Atlanta or New York, visit the art exhibits at the nearby Telfair Museum or Jepson Art Gallery. For a more contemporary take on visual art, the Julia Christian Gallery and the Savannah College of Art and Design's galleries sit within easy walking distance. To discover pieces of colonial history that you may have thought were lost to the mists of time forever, visit the Davenport House Museum, Georgia Historical Society or Georgia Railroad Museum. This property's location between East Liberty and East Oglethorpe puts it right near many interesting places. Probably the top one is Colonial Park Cemetery, which is just a short walk to the west down East Perry Lane. This historic cemetery opened in 1750 and became the final home to many of the city's earliest residents. In 1820, many victims of yellow fever ended up in this cemetery. The cemetery was closed to new burials before the beginning of the Civil War. It now has the appearance of a stately park with Spanish moss dripping from the old oaks. Right nearby the Habersham House is the Colonial Park Cemetery, which covers about six acres and is now more of a park, since it has been closed to new burials since the mid-1800s. Deep in the historic district is four renovated blocks that is now known as the City Market. This is one of the top visited places in downtown Savannah and features jazz clubs, restaurants, many open-air cafes, boutiques and gift shops. Another top attraction in Savannah is the 26 acres that constitutes Forsyth Park. Prominently featured in the well-known book and movie "Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil," this park really shines in the spring time when all the flowers are in bloom. The famous iron fountain completes the park known as the "pride of Savannah" and is modeled after a similar fountain in Paris. Another feature from the "Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil" book and film is Monterey Square and The Mercer House. This house is available for tours and also has a museum. A quick way to see Savannah is to take one of the many tours. You can choose from horse-drawn carriages, pedal-cabs and guided walking tours among others.
